statements.worth_reason: A partner's download count ('more than 200 million monthly downloads') is an ecosystem number that moves no NVIDIA revenue or share answer; the standard (D243 item 3) files ecosystem numbers as optional, so keeping it costs nothing in score but it only adds reading load for the judge.
statements.one_line_problem: Lost who said it: the one-line says 'LangChain reported', but the quote is an unattributed sentence in NVIDIA's own blog; it also adds the empty clause 'no period beyond monthly is specified'.
statements.tier_note: fact (a published figure stated in the item; it is not an analyst, media or expert opinion, so third_party_view is wrong)

statements.worth_reason: Named adopters (Abridge, Amdocs, Box, EY) of NVIDIA's agent blueprint with no size; the standard keeps named adoption without amount as supporting (D240), but for NVIDIA's revenue it is a logo list from its own marketing post.
Availability of a free software blueprint and a tuned model profile ('available now') has no business scale and is not a value-bearing product generation; it is product detail under 5.3 row 1.

grade_reason: A marketing post with nothing that changes an NVIDIA answer; the output writes three low-value records, and the one ecosystem number among them carries a wrong tier (third_party_view) and a one-line that credits LangChain with NVIDIA's sentence. Nothing material is missed: the '10x lower inference cost per run than leading closed models' line is a vendor benchmark claim the standard does not keep.
standard_doubt: Section 5.1 class 2 and D240 keep named adoption without amount as supporting ('一家软件公司把本公司的模型集成进政府系统' is kept; 后两条有名字、没金额，也留). Applied to a company's own marketing post, this makes every customer logo it lists ('Abridge, Amdocs and Box are embedding specialized agents directly into their platforms') a ledger record; for a company of NVIDIA's size an analyst would treat a vendor's self-reported logo list as noise unless the adopter is material or the item is an independent confirmation.
